floor_history.headline: Recon s1: floor re-measured 32 (chassis unchanged, all WIP-imported verdicts spendable); $v0/$v1 exchange confirmed at .greg disposition level (pseudo 100 in $v1, 83/84/98 in $v0); frontier = instrume

Structural respelling dropped the honest floor 32 -> 14 and RETRACTS the s1 'RA exchange validated unreachable' verdict: every $v0/$v1 hunk inverse.py had foreclosed closed under ordinary shared-named

Structural session: honest floor 14 -> 2 and build_insns now 231 == target 231; duplicating the tail addend and the >>12 into both use_high arms (sanctioned duplicated-statement-into-arms, merged back

Permuter measured dead on the floor-2 residual (3 chassis, ~45 min, ~35k iters, zero sub-60 finds) and control-flow exit forms proven inert; in exchange the divergence is now pinned exactly to sched2'

frontier.hypothesis: The only remaining handle on the sched.c:2461 tie-break is to make INSN_LUID(116) EXCEED INSN_LUID(140) in sched2's input stream (.greg order) WITHOUT changing the relative order of any memory operation - and since sched1 is the pass that normalises the chain below the three halfword stores, the lever is sched1's own ready-list decision, not source statement order.
frontier.mechanism: sched2 recomputes LUIDs from the .greg stream, which is sched1's output as re-registered by reload/global-alloc. s4 proved that moving the C expression does not change that stream because sched1 re-sinks the chain. So the question becomes: what property of the RTL makes sched1 rank the synth chain BELOW insns 116/119/122/124/127, and is that property source-reachable?
frontier.next_probe: FORENSICS modality: re-run `BB2_RANK_DEBUG=1 tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1 -O2 -G0 -funsigned-char -quiet -mcpu=3000 -mips1 -mno-abicalls -fno-builtin -w -mel tmp/grind/func_8001B748/s4/base.c -o /dev/null 2> rank.log` and read the FULL 145-line log (s4 only grepped for 116/140). Separate the sched1 decisions from the sched2 decisions, find every decision that places the synth chain relative to insn 116, and record whether each was decided by INSN_PRIORITY, by the class test, or by LUID. If a sched1 decision turns on PRIORITY, the lever is the chain's forward dependence length, which IS source-reachable; if it also turns on LUID, the whole displacement is LUID-locked and the function is a genuine sched-rank-class-tie wall (see .claude/rules/sched-rank-class-tie-wall.md).

frontier.hypothesis: Give insn 116 a strictly HIGHER INSN_PRIORITY than insn 140 so the sched2 comparator returns at its first test and never reaches the class test or the LUID tie-break.
frontier.mechanism: priority() in sched.c is the longest path to the end of the block through INSN_DEPEND forward links. Insn 116's forward path runs through the anti/output-dependent memory chain (119 -> 531 -> 127 -> 122/124 -> the dst+0x18 store). If the store had a longer forward dependence chain - or the synth chain a shorter one - the priority comparison would decide the pair and LUID would never be consulted. This is the one axis s4 did NOT probe: s4's variants only moved source position, which changes LUID and live ranges but not the dependence graph's shape.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate honest C changes that LENGTHEN the gp store's forward memory-dependence chain without changing emitted memory order - e.g. a read-back of D_800A3310 somewhere the function already needs its value, or reordering only among the dst halfword stores that follow it - and score each with tmp/grind/func_8001B748/s4/score.py (~2 s per variant). If the source-level sweep is inconclusive, instrument priority() the same way rank_for_schedule already is (a BB2_PRIO_DEBUG print of INSN_UID/INSN_PRIORITY per insn); that reveals the exact priority gap to close and whether it is 1 or 10.

frontier.hypothesis: The residual is a two-insn ORDERING-ONLY difference at build_insns == target_insns == 231 with every other byte matching, which makes it the archetype of the frozen sched-rank-class-tie wall - so if both probes above come back LUID-locked, the correct next step is a disposition entry, not more spelling search.
frontier.mechanism: Four distinct axes have now measured this hunk dead: s2/s3 statement order (85 orders, min 2, 19 ties), s3 expression shape, s4 randomised permuter search (~35k iterations, 3 chassis), and s4 control-flow form. s4 attributes the divergence to a single comparator line whose deciding term is INSN_LUID - a quantity source order provably cannot move here, because sched1 normalises it before sched2 sees it.
frontier.next_probe: Do NOT spend a session re-measuring the four dead axes. Run the two forensics probes above first. Only if BOTH confirm the LUID lock should a session consider the endgame-lock gates - and note that scan_hand_coded's tier for this function has NOT been measured in this grind, so it must be measured before it can be cited, and the owner's standing 2026-07-27 ruling requires the DRIVER to have declared exhaustion (escalation modality) before any disposition is written.
